targets.function: RNA-dependent RNA polymerase that performs primer-template recognition and RNA synthesis during viral replication. Initiates RNA transcription/replication at a flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD), resulting in a 5'- FAD cap on viral RNAs. In this way, recognition of viral 5' RNA by host pattern recognition receptors can be bypassed, thereby evading activation of antiviral pathways

targets.function: Cysteine protease required for the proteolytic auto-cleavage between the non-structural proteins NS2 and NS3 (By similarity). The N-terminus of NS3 is required for the function of NS2 protease (active region NS2-3) (By similarity). Promotes the initiation of viral particle assembly by mediating the interaction between structural and non-structural proteins (By similarity)
targets.assembles_into: Homodimer (By similarity). Interacts with envelope glycoprotein E1 (By similarity). Interacts with envelope glycoprotein E2 (By similarity). Interacts with viroporin p7 (By similarity). Interacts with serine protease/helicase NS3 (By similarity). Part of the replication complex composed of NS2, NS3, NS4A, NS4B, NS5A and the RNA-directed RNA polymerase embedded in an ER-derived membranous web (By similarity). Part of the viral assembly initiation complex composed of NS2, E1, E2, NS3, NS4A, NS5A and the core protein (By similarity)

targets.function: Displays three enzymatic activities: serine protease with a chymotrypsin-like fold, NTPase and RNA helicase (PubMed:10497107). NS3 serine protease, in association with NS4A, is responsible for the cleavages of NS3-NS4A, NS4A-NS4B, NS4B-NS5A and NS5A-NS5B (By similarity). The NS3/NS4A complex prevents phosphorylation of host IRF3, thus preventing the establishment of dsRNA induced antiviral state (By similarity). NS3 RNA helicase binds to RNA and unwinds both dsDNA and dsRNA in the 3' to 5' direction, and likely resolves RNA complicated stable secondary structures in the template strand (By similarity). Cleaves host MAVS/CARDIF thereby preventing the establishment of an antiviral state (PubMed:17093192)
targets.assembles_into: Interacts with protease NS2 (By similarity). Interacts with non-structural protein 4A; this interaction stabilizes the folding of NS3 serine protease (By similarity). NS3-NS4A interaction is essential for NS3 activation and allows membrane anchorage of the latter (By similarity). Interacts with host MAVS; this interaction leads to the cleavage and inhibition of host MAVS (Probable). Part of the replication complex composed of NS2, NS3, NS4A, NS4B, NS5A and the RNA-directed RNA polymerase embedded in an ER-derived membranous web (By similarity). Part of the viral assembly initiation complex composed of NS2, E1, E2, NS3, NS4A, NS5A and the core protein (By similarity)

targets.not_annotated_because: this chain was identified with no reviewed relative, so there is no curated entry to read a function from

limitations: No row here is a measurement on the pathogen. Function, families, partners and marked residues are curated annotation on the nearest reviewed relative, transferred across a species gap. A deposited area is measured on a relative's domain; a predicted area is measured on coordinates a model emitted.

An area measured on predicted coordinates is comparable with another prediction and not with a deposition. On the one chain carrying both, the prediction read several times larger. Residue positions transfer far better than areas do.

A nucleotide range appears only where the reading frame was settled. `nt_confirmed_at` says how. Most chains are their reading frame's whole translation, were never cut out of a polyprotein and cross no species gap, so their coordinate is exact by construction. A chain that was cut out of one is placed by alignment and its frame is confirmed by reading the residues back against the relative; there `nt_confirmed_at` names which end of the span that covered, because a chain spanning a ribosomal frameshift can be exact at one end and short at the other.

`residues_in_the_chain` is 1-based within the mature chain and is the numbering for a structure viewer. `residues_in_the_reading_frame` is 1-based along one reading frame of this genome and is meaningless without the frame in the same row.
A cleavage site is where this protein is cut. It is a marked residue and it is not somewhere to bind.

The ranking is the pipeline's five stated weights. Fitting those weights against the proteins approved antivirals already act on does not improve them, which is recorded in runs/rubric_fit.json; the ranking is carried by the terms rather than their weighting.

`already_drugged` marks a target an approved or late-stage antiviral acts on, which is the label set this pipeline is scored against. It is not a claim that the target is easy, and an unmarked target is not a claim that it is novel.
